disclaimer: This report lists observations about a codebase. Not an assessment of compliance with any regulation. Risk classification under the EU AI Act is a legal determination made by the operator, not a tool output. Every rule in this report is UNMEASURED: no precision figure exists for it yet. Absence of a finding is not evidence of safety.

findings.title: Emotion or biometric inference on persons

evidence.snippet: - **No Implicit Attribute Inference**: Don't infer gender, age, ethnicity, etc. from names or context. Only record explicitly stated attributes.

recommendation.summary: Remove the inference or restrict it to a documented, lawful use with a legal basis and an Annex III review; emotion recognition at work or in education and biometric categorisation of protected characteristics are listed practices under Art. 5.
alternatives: remove the inference or restrict it to a medical or safety use with a documented legal basis
replace emotion inference with explicit, user-stated preferences
an Annex III conformity review before deployment
aisafe: nothing here applies; the control is removing or scoping the inference

known_failure_modes: text-only sentiment analysis is not counted: the EU definition of emotion recognition rests on biometric data
a library imported for a demo counts as use; DetectFaces without Emotions does not
whether the inference happens in a workplace or an education setting is read from the lint rule's words (employee, student), not from the deployment
findings.notes: inference of a protected characteristic from a person (- **No Implicit Attribute Inference**: Don't infer gender, age, ethnicity, etc. from names or context. Only record explicitly stated attributes.). Whether this practice falls under Art. 5, Art. 50 or Annex III of Regulation (EU) 2024/1689 is a legal determination made by the operator, not a tool output. The finding reports what the code and the prompts say.

findings.title: Person profile bound into a prompt

evidence.snippet: prompt = f"""You are a fitness assistant who helps Anish with his training, recovery, and diet. You have long-term memory of his health, routines, preference...

recommendation.summary: Pass the model only the fields the task needs. A behavioural profile in the prompt is personal data processed for a new purpose; drop it, reduce it, or pseudonymise it and document the lawful basis.
alternatives: drop the profile from the prompt and pass only the fields the task needs
pseudonymise with PIIDetector(action="tokenize") and restore on output
document the lawful basis and purpose in a DPIA next to the prompt
Microsoft Presidio or LLM Guard Anonymize on the ingress path

package.leaves_open: PIIDetector(action="tokenize") removes the entity types it knows from the prompt; a behavioural profile has no entity type and stays in the prompt until it is left out or reduced by hand. ManipulationGuard reads the response, not the profile.

known_failure_modes: the NAME is the signal: a `preferences` variable may hold a UI theme, and a profile fetched at runtime under a neutral name is missed
`conversation_history` and the other transcript names are excluded by design
grouped per unit, sub-finding and file, anchored on the first site by path
findings.notes: profile `preferences` read above is bound into the prompt assembled here. Whether this practice falls under Art. 5, Art. 50 or Annex III of Regulation (EU) 2024/1689 is a legal determination made by the operator, not a tool output. The finding reports what the code and the prompts say.

findings.title: Scoring, ranking or automated decision about persons

evidence.snippet: def onboarding_complete(body: OnboardingCompleteRequest, user: User = Depends(require_auth)):

recommendation.summary: Put a human review step before any score, rank or decision about a person takes effect, log the recommendation beside the decision, and record the use on the system card.
alternatives: a human review step before any decision about a person takes effect, logged beside the recommendation
ToolPolicyGuard(require_approval=[...], approval_callback=...) when the decision is a tool
a confidence threshold routing low-confidence cases to review
Fairlearn or AIF360 evaluation of the scoring model

package.leaves_open: ToolPolicyGuard gates only a decision dispatched through run_processing as a tool call with a real approval_callback. A score computed and acted on in plain code is not on that path.

known_failure_modes: credit scoring is an Annex III use, not a prohibited one; the finding says what co-occurred and the card decides the category
a risk score of a transaction is not a person score: the person noun is required on the same line or inside the same prompt literal
`approve_refund` is not a decision about a person; a decision function is reported only when its body names a person and no review symbol
findings.notes: an automated decision function names a person and no review or approval symbol in its body (EU-AIA-014a). findings.title: No manipulation control on the response path

evidence.snippet: unit u0 takes user input, calls a model and carries person signals (profile_name), and no manipulation or disclosure control symbol appears in its code or co...

recommendation.summary: Put a manipulation and disclosure control on the output stage and measure it: ManipulationGuard flags influence tactics, AIDisclosureGuard flags human claims.
alternatives: aisafe ManipulationGuard and AIDisclosureGuard on output, then aisafe measure
LLM Guard output scanners for banned topics plus a judge

findings.title: AI nature concealed or no disclosure on the response path

evidence.snippet: unit u3 takes user input and calls a model, and no disclosure symbol (an AI-assistant statement, transparency_disclosure, ai_disclosure_output) appears in it...

recommendation.summary: Delete any instruction to claim humanity and state the AI nature at first interaction and whenever asked; AIDisclosureGuard flags a response that claims to be human and can append the disclosure on the output stage.
alternatives: delete the instruction and state the AI nature at first interaction
aisafe AIDisclosureGuard(disclosure=..., append_when="on_claim")
NeMo Guardrails AI-identity flow
a UI banner at session start plus a disclosure on every channel the bot speaks through

package.leaves_open: AIDisclosureGuard flags a response that claims to be human and can append the disclosure text on the output stage; a prompt that instructs the model to claim humanity is deleted by hand, and disclosure shown by the UI is outside the guard.

known_failure_modes: a named persona (Ava) is not concealment; the regex needs a human claim or a concealment verb
a disclosure delivered by the UI rather than the code is reported as absent
the no-disclosure sub-finding is unit-level and LOW: it says no disclosure symbol was found, not that none is shown
findings.notes: unit u3 takes user input and calls a model, and no disclosure symbol (an AI-assistant statement, transparency_disclosure, ai_disclosure_output) appears in its code, config or prompt files. rules.title: Agent loop without an iteration cap
Fetch/browse tool without a URL allowlist
Irreversible tool with no approval gate
Irreversible tool without a dry-run or idempotency affordance
LETHAL TRIFECTA: private data + untrusted content + external action in one scope
Untrusted content concatenated into a prompt
System prompt built from request data
Secret or PII bound into a prompt
Literal PII in prompts / fixtures / logs
LLM judge without credentials or timeout
Reported guard over the declared budget
Probe report shows failed, inconclusive, errored or skipped cases
Annex III keywords in prompt material, no category on the card
Person profile bound into a prompt
Emotion or biometric inference on persons
Scoring, ranking or automated decision about persons
Engagement or retention objective in prompt or code
AI nature concealed or no disclosure on the response path
No manipulation control on the response path
Prompt and algorithm audit not recorded
No crisis path where a person confides in the AI
